asked_by: Madhav, 26 Oct 2026 (India chat): "we have to do research about this FII and their influence on the stock prices"
title: Foreign investor (FPI) cash flows: do sharp outflows precede a weaker Nifty, and inflows a stronger one?
hypothesis: Sessions after sharply negative FPI equity net flows (bottom decile, daily or over 5 sessions) are followed by weaker Nifty returns over 1, 5 and 20 sessions; after sharply positive flows (top decile) by stronger returns.

data.flows: silver/flows/fii_dii_cash.parquet, category FPI_equity (NSDL archive: custodians' daily equity buy/sell/net in Rs crore, by reporting date), 2000-2023; filled 25 Oct 2026 by india/fiidii.py

timing: NSDL rows are dated by reporting date; a row is first used at the first Nifty session on or after its reporting date, and the index outcome runs from the NEXT session's close (so the flow is known a full session before any entry)

definitions.neg1 / pos1: the day's FPI equity net in the bottom / top decile of its own trailing 756-session distribution (threshold known at the time; flows grow with the market, so a fixed rupee cut-off would be wrong)
definitions.neg5 / pos5: the 5-session sum in the bottom / top decile of its trailing 756-session distribution

outcomes: nfwd1 / nfwd5 / nfwd20: Nifty from the next session's close
statistics: india.teachers_stock.msplit (market timing: quarter blocks of 'on' against 'off' sessions, Welch t); development 2003-2017, validation 2018-2023; india/registry.record standard rule, MIN_DATES 16

bar.note: family 'flows' already holds C06's 4 rows; k frozen at 4 + the 8 variants below

descriptive_only: TWT-H48 (FII flow beta, before and after the SIP era): the same-day sensitivity of the Nifty's return to the FPI net flow (in units of the trailing flow spread), by year and for 2003-2016 against 2017-2023. Same-day, so not a trading rule and not a registered verdict.
not_claimed: No paper rule changes from this study.
